# Retained player creation and persistence acceptance

The reproduction driver copies the latest player's domain, formal build,
snapshot, and selected conversation into an independent hidden test profile.
Original files and databases are read only. Scheduled tasks must be absent;
the credential store is not copied. The sealed application executes the real
Godot PCK and dispatches the existing protected interact action. Bound images
and before/after snapshots record whether pickup actually occurred.

The natural follow-up driver restores the same conversation through normal
F2 presentation and uses the original Composer callbacks. Before input and
send it verifies the selected session. The original model, thinking level,
and permission mode are retained. Credentials needed by the isolated copy
are installed through the normal provider API, followed by a normal restart.
It does not manually accept permissions, check, adopt, or alter generated code.

No extra model-call, token, repair-round, or whole-run deadline is imposed.
A cancellation file and signals stop the run normally. Transport timeouts
remain distinct from model budgets. Errors and intermediate failed attempts
are retained, including execution-path limits and pre-model TURN_ENDED.

Only a different formal build, actual automatic handoff, and save/reopen can
complete a modification-flow report. Generated gameplay still needs separate
actual interaction evidence; a build check or model statement alone is not
proof that E pickup, equipment, or persistent ammunition works.

With the two-card entry, retained acceptance selects a card only if its
host-provided world ID exactly matches the expected existing world. Otherwise
it returns to the current legacy world or opens that exact world through
advanced saves. It must not select a same-engine replacement slot or create
a new world and lose the retained draft. The driver records which visible
entry route it used and checks the actual runtime world/build afterwards.
Independent decision tests cover exact identity, loading, legacy, and return
paths. Native integration remains pending the next package and exclusive slot.

The prompt-response diagnostic wraps the existing main IPC handler only to
record its returned error. It forwards the original arguments and result,
does not modify authorization, and runs only in the isolated hidden owner.

Validation at this commit: both driver syntax checks passed; sealed 125f
reproduction confirmed failed pickup at 0.726 metres with actual interact
dispatch and a clean native exit. Subsequent ordinary modification wrote
revision 6, but path-length and then TURN_ENDED preconditions prevented its
adoption. Those failures remain preserved, not presented as passed gameplay.

## September 13 completed continuation and gameplay evidence

The ordinary continuation driver now waits for the real prompt IPC admission
receipt before interpreting turn metrics. A narrowly identified
`CREATION_PLAYER_CONTEXT_CHANGED` read during binding is pending, not a prompt
rejection; other errors are retained. The `saved` runtime status is not a pause
signal. Automatic handoff accepts ready/saved only with the same world/build/
instance and advancing actual physics ticks, with no injected resume.

The retained pickup continuation used the original Flash/max/auto binding and
four real model calls, adopted the existing model-authored revision 6, and
completed ordinary save/reopen. Original player data remained read-only.
`tests/godot-player-result-gameplay.mjs` verified the same formal result in the
final 03bc package twice: actual E, unchanged inventory on repeat E, dialogue
rejection (`PLAY_ACTION_PAUSED`), exact snapshot preservation and clean exits.
`tests/pickup-weapon-engine.mjs` separately verified the exact exported source
manifest in pinned Godot: 14 checks plus a new process restoring noninitial
29/116 ammunition. This is engine gameplay evidence, not packaged physical
mouse firing. Generated source is never modified by these drivers.

`tests/export-repaired-world.mjs` and `tests/verify-restored-world.mjs` use the
formal portable backup APIs. The resulting complete isolated-domain archive
includes source, history and progress, excludes credentials, and restored into
a new empty domain with the same formal build. It is not a single-world export
or a modification of the original player profile. The exact report, failed
harness attempts and byte proofs are indexed in the ignored
`ordinary-followup-GwAWlm/acceptance-index.json` evidence artifact.
